This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Direct absolute/systemic oral bioavailability measurements in the gold contexts all exceed the 20% threshold: metolazone approximately 100% and 60–80% (C25, C42, C61), valdecoxib 83% (C01, C08, C11), meloxicam 91% (C03), pritelivir 75% (C26), ixazomib 58–60% (C05, C09, C28), PF-05241328 38% (C04, C14), amlodipine 58% (C21), and 2,4-D nearly complete (C18, C40, C52).

The query is a 4-chloro-5-sulfamoyl salicylanilide; the metolazone context is the closest structural gold context. L5 C174 shows metolazone has Caco-2 P_c 610×10^-8 cm/s with FA=64%, and C185 shows it is a BCRP substrate, yet metolazone's direct F is high, so efflux substrate status does not establish F < 20%.

L5 efflux/intestinal-metabolism records for sulpiride (C218, C209, C176), furosemide (C182, C191, C207, C213), chlorothiazide (C199, C175), and hydrochlorothiazide (C219, C195) are mechanistic measurements for other molecules; none reports an F value for the query or provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20%.

The only subthreshold direct context, celecoxib 20–40% (C13), is explicitly attributed to poor aqueous solubility and does not transfer to this ionized salicylanilide (logD 0.7, acidic pKa 5.54, neutral fraction 0.01).

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule (a 4-chloro-5-sulfamoyl salicylanilide).

No query-specific gut-wall efflux or intestinal metabolism data are available; L5 records are for furosemide, sulpiride, metolazone, chlorothiazide, hydrochlorothiazide, and other molecules, not the query.
L5 efflux records do not report F values and cannot establish whether any presystemic loss would reduce F below 20%.
No query-specific first-pass or systemic clearance data exist; possible phenol/amide/sulfonamide conjugation is speculative without evidence.
Transfer from the metolazone context is structural but not identity; metolazone is a cyclic quinazolinone, while the query is an open salicylanilide.
content.decision_summary: L5 adds only mechanistic gut-wall efflux/intestinal-metabolism records for other sulfonamide-containing molecules. The closest structural gold context, metolazone, has high direct F despite BCRP substrate status (C174, C185, C25/C42/C61), and no L5 record provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20% in the query. Prediction remains high for F >= 20% with moderate confidence.
